extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: A video-based question-answering dataset for robotic task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction across 16 tasks and 53 scenes in simulation and real-world environments. It contains 9,440 failure trajectories, 1,282 successful trajectories, and 78,623 QA pairs covering eight question types and six failure categories across task planning, motion planning, and execution control.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
extraction.citeAs: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, and Bo Zhao. RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv:2505.12224v3 [cs.RO], 25 May 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Simulation data were collected for 14 robotic tasks in ManiSkill, augmented with YCB objects and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Expert policies specified target end-effector poses for each substage, with motion planning generating feasible trajectories. Failure trajectories were generated by replacing the expert policy at a selected substage with an erroneous code snippet. Videos were recorded alongside descriptions of the failure substage, failure category, error details, and perturbed poses where applicable. Real-world data for six tasks were collected through teleoperation of an SO-100 robotic arm, with corresponding textual descriptions. Successful trajectories were also collected to prevent overfitting to failure patterns. The final collection includes 8,960 simulated and 480 real-world failure trajectories, plus 1,160 simulated and 122 real-world successful trajectories.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Software Collection, Physical data collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Robot manipulation videos and their associated textual descriptions from ManiSkill simulations and teleoperated SO-100 robotic arm executions. Simulation assets include objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Descriptions record failure types, error substages, detailed error explanations, and perturbed end-effector poses for pose-related failures.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Failure trajectories were generated by replacing an expert policy with an erroneous code snippet at a selected substage, including perturbations to end-effector poses. Object categories, environmental scenes, backgrounds, and camera viewpoints were varied. Five phrasings were authored for each question type, and one template was randomly sampled when constructing each QA pair.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Simulation motion planning occasionally failed, producing trajectories inconsistent with the associated textual descriptions. The authors manually cleaned the collected data and retained approximately 75%.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Videos were annotated with eight QA types: task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating, failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction. Reference answers for the first five types were extracted directly from the associated textual descriptions. For failure explanation and high- and low-level correction, GPT-4o received the video and a prompt constructed from its description, including task, subtasks, failure type, error stage, error details, correction suggestions, and perturbation information. The prompt required qualitative descriptions rather than specific numerical values. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The authors treated five question types as having well-defined ground truths extractable from the recorded descriptions. For the three question types generated by GPT-4o, all outputs underwent manual review and correction to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Fine-tuning multimodal models for robotic task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction; benchmarking robotic failure video understanding; evaluating visual generalization, sim-to-real transfer, and generalization to unseen tasks. The training set consists of approximately 60,000 randomly sampled simulated QA pairs. Evaluation uses the remaining approximately 10,000 simulated QA pairs and 8,000 real-world QA pairs. The simulated test split contains over 1,000 videos entirely unseen during training, and the real-world test split includes two tasks absent from simulation training: InsertCylinder and PlaceCube. Models trained on the dataset are also used as external critics that provide natural-language recovery instructions to VLA-controlled robots.
